title: 本草綱目拾遺(一)
shelf_note: Zhao Xuemin's 1765 supplement to the Bencao gangmu. The page is Chinese materia medica (remedies, lotus-leaf dew), so it belongs in a general Chinese/universal collection.
structure_note: The structure counts say pages_translated 0, but the book field says 99, and this page carries a translation. That is a counting discrepancy (E2), not a defect on the page. Only 1 page has a printed number, which fits a Chinese print whose foliation sits in the block-heart: on this leaf the block-heart is cut off at the right edge. There are no backsteps or repeats.

ocr_errors.image: printed (woodblock/type) characters in a ruled frame
ocr_errors.problem: The self-reported script tag is wrong. It is not shown as reading text.

tr_errors.source: 將長杓坐碗於首向荷池葉上傾瀉之
tr_errors.english: take a long ladle with a bowl set at its head and tip the lotus leaves over the pond to pour the dew into it
tr_errors.problem: The source has the ladle-and-bowl reaching toward the lotus leaves on the pond, and the dew is tipped from the leaves into it. 'tip the lotus leaves over the pond' is a loose, slightly confusing rendering, but the sense can be recovered.
This is a word-for-word rendering of an obscure disease name. The quotation marks flag it, but nothing explains it, so the heading means nothing to a reader.

pages.layout: ten vertical columns between ruled lines, inside a heavy single-line frame. Entry heads (荷葉上露) are set as their own columns. The block-heart is cut off at the right edge.

items.quote: original: "喉蛾", swelling of the throat

missing.why: The disease name makes no sense in English. The reader needs to be told that the term is obscure, or what condition is probably meant.
'Water-drum' (水臌) is a technical term from Chinese medicine for abdominal dropsy or ascites. Without a gloss the reader cannot tell what the dew treats.

missing.english: mixed with a little holy water
missing.why: 'Holy water' (聖水) is an odd ingredient in a Chinese recipe. A reader needs a note on what the term refers to here.
The literal plant name gives no clue which plant is meant. A short note saying it is a folk name, unidentified or identified, would help.
These words stand alone at the foot of the page. The reader needs to be told that this entry continues on the next page.

book_verdict: The transcription matches the leaf character for character, and the translation is faithful, with only small looseness in the dew-gathering passage. The notes are accurate but mostly just repeat the original characters, while the medical terms a reader needs explained ('water-drum', 'holy water', 'eating hundred urine') get none.
